body:
Alright, reading again I think I am beginning to see. It looks like Claude is (rightly) playing language lawyer. The C++ spec states that an implicitly-created object's  (that is, one not introduced by a `new` expression) lifetime must begin in an `operator new`. Consequently, the previous implementation was strictly-speaking incorrect: it allocated storage but failed to actually begin the lifetime of the object residing in that storage.

Previously this was perhaps okay since the storage held POD, but now it contains a `v_vnni_tensor`, requiring that we be a bit more careful.

I think it would be good to reword the Note more clearly.

+#include "tron/tensor/view.hpp"
+
+// Note [Packed V layout]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// In the 16-lane (AVX-512) build the V plane of a kv_block stores token pairs
+// interleaved: for each dimension d, the values of tokens 2p and 2p + 1 sit
+// next to each other. With D dimensions per token, element (token, d) is at
+//
+//   plane[(token / 2) * (2 * D) + 2 * d + token % 2]      (in bf16 elements)
+//
+// so one "pair row" of 2 * D bf16 holds two whole tokens. One 64-byte vector
+// load at pair_base + 2 * 16 * i yields dims [16 * i, 16 * i + 16) of both tokens.
+// In every 32-bit lane the even token sits in the low 16 bits and the odd token
+// in the high 16 bits. That is the B-operand layout of the bf16 dot product
+// instructions (VDPBF16PS and the AMX tile multiply). The weighted sum
+// (detail::scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp) and the AMX PV kernel
+// (amx_attn_h128g4::weights_times_v_128x4) therefore read the plane in place.
+//
+// The 8-lane (AVX2) build keeps V row-major and does not use these types for
+// storage. The classes are still defined there, so that declarations naming
+// them (the AMX kernel signatures and their CPU fakes) compile. The vector
+// operations and the row expression's chunk reads exist only at 16 lanes.
+//
+// Who may compute a packed address: the row expression (v_vnni_row), the
+// typed operations in this header, and the two layout-specific kernels named
+// above, which reach the plane through detail::v_vnni_access. Cache code, the
+// model, hardware staging and the tests use the typed operations or the page
+// accessors built on them (page::set_v, page::get_v, page::append_v,
+// page::v_packed). book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills
+// a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates.
+//
+// Writing rules are the cache's: see Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] in
+// kv_cache.hpp. In short, appending an even token also zeroes its odd partner,
+// and appending an odd token merges into an initialized pair. Direct element
+// writes through a view (at(), row[dim]) do neither; they serve fixtures.
+
+namespace tron {
+
+namespace detail {
+// The one route from a packed view to its plane address, for the two
+// layout-specific kernels (Note [Packed V layout]) and the operations below.
+struct v_vnni_access;
+}  // namespace detail
+
+// Two tokens share one pair row of the packed plane.
+inline constexpr size_t V_PAIR_TOKENS_2 = 2;
+
+// Byte alignment of one packed V plane. In the 16-lane build every pair chunk is
+// one 64-byte vector load, and the AMX PV kernel reads the plane in 64-byte tile
+// rows. Fixed for both lane counts (chunk_alignment is 32 bytes at 8 lanes).
+inline constexpr size_t V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64 = 64;
+
+// page::set_v and page::get_v have always required head_size % 32 == 0. The
+// moved loops step one chunk (16 dims) at a time and do not need it. The
+// constraint stays so that the accepted row widths do not change.
+inline constexpr size_t V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 = 32;
+
+// Width of one stored bf16 value: the shift that moves a value between the
+// low (even token) and the high (odd token) half of a 32-bit lane.
+inline constexpr unsigned BF16_BITS_16 = 16;
+
+// Lane masks selecting the odd (high half) or the even (low half) token.
+inline constexpr int V_ODD_TOKEN_LANE_MASK_0XFFFF0000 = static_cast<int>(0xffff0000u);
+inline constexpr int V_EVEN_TOKEN_LANE_MASK_0X0000FFFF = 0x0000ffff;
+
+template <typename T>
+concept v_vnni_element = std::same_as<T, bf16> || std::same_as<T, const bf16>;
+
+// One logical row (one token's Cols dimensions) of a packed V plane, read as a
+// rank-1 expression (the rank is the number of indices: row[dim] takes one).
+// Only v_vnni_view::operator[] constructs rows. A row keeps its pair address

+// yields read-only elements.
+template <typename T, size_t Cols>
+struct v_vnni_row final : expr<v_vnni_row<T, Cols>, Cols> {
